text:
tasha: Running into a typing pain in the Python sampleapp with paginated endpoints. The autogen stubs type `client.items.paginate()` as `Paginator` with no generics so editors and mypy/pyright treat yielded items as `Any`. New hires are blocked when strict checks expect `.id`/`.name` attributes.

mike: Ugh. Can you paste a minimal repro + which checker/version?

tasha: repro (mypy 1.9.0, pyright strict):
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key='x')

async def drain():
    async for item in client.items.paginate(limit=10):
        # runtime: item is a Mapping[str, Any] with 'id' key
        print(item['id'])  # mypy: "Item has type 'Any'" or no completions in VSCode
```

tasha: Runtime yields typed dicts but our pyi emits an unparameterized `class Paginator:` with `def __aiter__(self) -> 'AsyncIterator':`. Codegen dropped the concrete element type.

yuri: This is a generator-generic problem in the pyi templates. We should make the paginator generic: `T = TypeVar('T')` then `class Paginator(Generic[T]): def __aiter__(self) -> AsyncIterator[T]: ...` and have autogen wire the element type from the endpoint schema. That gives consumers `AsyncIterator[ItemModel]` or `AsyncIterator[Mapping[str, Any]]`.

mike: Sounds good. Any compatibility risk? Old checkers that don't support generics might still be fine if we provide a non-generic fallback or default TypeVar bound to Any.

yuri: Right — emit `T = TypeVar('T', bound=Any)` and keep `Paginator(Generic[T])`. Most modern mypy/pyright versions handle this. Also we should update streaming vs paging: stream() already returns `AsyncIterator[ChatChunk]` in newer stubs; paginate should match that pattern.

tasha: Will this also help editor completions so new hires see fields when iterating?

yuri: Yes. If we point the pyi generator at the model class or Mapping type, editors will show keys/attrs. We'll also need to ensure autogen resolves inline schemas to a typed alias so the pyi references a single symbol rather than inlining an anonymous Mapping type.

mike: Plan: 1) change pyi paginator template to be generic and wire the element type, 2) add a mypy+pyright test in sampleapp that iterates and accesses `.id`, 3) add a tiny doc snippet showing annotated `async for item in client.items.paginate() -> Item` usage and a migration note. I'll open an issue and assign eng-ml.

tasha: Thanks. This is blocking the onboarding lab where everyone runs strict type checks on the sampleapp.

devx-bot: Issue created: #3358 by @mike 
https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3358 :white_check_mark:

mike: I'll take the autogen template PR, include tests, and propose a backport to the current release branch used by the onboarding image.

yuri: I'll help with the pyi wiring in autogen so the element type is resolved to the declared response model or Mapping alias.

tasha: Awesome, thanks both. This should make the iterator typing feel first-class for new engineers.
